Haworth Scouring was founded in 1966 in Haworth, UK. In 1998, Haworth Scouring moved 14 miles to its current location today on a purpose built 8 acre site in the heart of the textile industry in the UK. Haworth scouring is one of the largest capacity duel set wool scours in the world. The two sets can scour up to 1,000 tonnes per week and can scour wool comfortably at a rate of 3.5 tonnes per hour. In addition to this high technology scouring process, the site also features a state of the art effluent treatment plant. In 2002, Curtis Wool Direct purchased a 50% shareholding in Haworth Scouring and Haworth Combing companies and six years later acquired the remaining 50% to take full ownership of both companies. One year later in 2009, Curtis Wool Direct acquired Enco Global testing. Curtis Wool Direct have invested heavily into all areas of the site, maintaining Haworth Scouring as a world leader in wool processing whilst adhering to more stringent regulations in relation to effluent and maintaining its excellent ‘green’ credentials. A multi-million GBP investment in state of the art Schlumberger Era combing machinery was completed in late 2017 giving Haworth Combing the capacity to produce up to 150,000kgs wool tops per week and to comb wools from 22µm – 40µm. At the same time, Enco Global Testing has purchased modern equipment able to detect the smallest qualities of compounds found in effluents not solely related to the Textile Industry but all sectors of business where environmental waste is a concern. The Haworth site is state of the art, producing high quality scoured wool, wool tops and a vast array of environmental and textile related testing requirements. Sitemap. Contact. Privacy Policy.

MEASURING LUSTROUS FIBRES – RAMPISHAM HILL MILL. Skip to content. RAMPISHAM HILL MILL. Menu. Close. MEASURING LUSTROUS FIBRES. Measuring the staple length of your fibre correctly is paramount, as it can dictate which processing options will be available for you and your type of fibre. It is particularly important that this measurement is done accurately for lustrous breeds such as: Cotswold, Gotland, Romney, Teeswater, Wensleydale, Leicester Longwool, Lincoln Longwool, Valais Blacknose, Grey Faced Dartmoor, Devon & Cornwall Longwool, as well as cross breeds with longer fibres etc. When we ask for the staple length of your fibre we need the length of those fibres when they are fully teased out and then stretched taut. As you can see from the photograph above, which is of some Wensleydale fibre, there is an 8.5cm (3½ inch) difference between the ‘perceived to be’ stretched fibre example measurement of 17.5cm (7 inch) and the true fibre staple length which is actually 26cm (10 ¼ inch) when fully teased out taut, as seen in the bottom example. When asked, customers would typically tell us the staple length of this example Wensleydale fibre is 17.5cm (7 inch), however you can see there are still a lot of visible loops and curls of individual fibres running within the lock, as even though a few of the shorter fibres look parallel and might be stretched taut, the majority are not, hence the much lower staple length measurement. TOP TIPS FOR MAKING ACCURATE MEASUREMENTS OF STAPLE LENGHT. To measure your fibre’s staple length accurately please randomly select a few locks from various parts of the fleece or consignment. Find at least a 30cm (12 inch) ruler or a tape measure and put it flat on a surface ready to take a measurement after you have prepared your fibre. Get a small clump of one of those locks, holding the tip firmly between your fingers, gently tease those individual fibres out of the lock by running your other hand down the lock from top to bottom while keeping hold of the tip. You might have to repeat this a few times to really get tease out the ‘tangles’ and end up with smooth parallel fibres. Some fibre breakage is inevitable while you are doing this and these might then ‘recoil’ back into their original shape, but try to keep it to a minimum as you want the longest fibres possible. You can see in the bottom example above that there are still a few curls where the shorter fibres within have recoiled as they are not being held at both ends, but the longer fibres are now parallel and held taut. Once you have a drawn out the fibres from the lock satisfactorily, hold the tip again and then, gently slide your other hand down lightly pinching the fibre as to keep a little bit of tension on the fibres, do this until you are just holding them by the very ends, then while the fibre is still taut take a measurement on your ruler or tape measure, remembering to include the bit of fibre held in between your fingers! It is good practice to repeat this exercise for locks from different parts of the fleece or the consignment as this will then give an average staple length and a maximum staple length of that fleece or consignment. Once you get the hang of the technique it doesn’t take long to take the measurements, but it will really help us to help you if you can supply an accurate staple length. If you have any questions regarding measuring your fibre then please do not hesitate to contact us.

Wingham Wool Work began over 40 years ago in the rolling hills of Yorkshire, founded by Ruth and Alan, whose love for wool inspired them to share the very best fibres with spinners and crafters. From a small, family-run operation, the business grew steadily, earning a reputation across the UK for quality, care, and a deep understanding of fibres. For decades, Ruth and Alan nurtured every aspect of the business, from selecting the finest British wools to sourcing luxurious silks, alpaca, and rare blends. Their dedication created a foundation built on trust, craftsmanship, and a passion for natural fibres — a foundation that continues to shape Wingham Wool Work today. In recent years, the next generation has stepped forward. Tom and Ellie now run the day-to-day operations, taking the business into a new chapter while Ruth and Alan step back. With the move to the picturesque Gloucestershire countryside, Tom and Ellie have grown the business with the help of a talented and dedicated team, whose expertise and commitment ensure that every fibre, fleece, and product meets the high standards Wingham Wool Work is known for. Every fibre we offer is carefully chosen with attention to quality, sustainability, and versatility. Our mission remains simple: to provide exceptional fibres and materials that celebrate the natural beauty of wool, honour our heritage, and keep the family tradition alive. Our expertise, which now spans more than 30 years, has enabled us to become a major player in the world textile industry. We aim to know about every kind of textile fibres available, where to source it at the most competitive price, anticipating customer demand and stocking a range of fibres to meet their requirements. With our stock-holding capability, combined with our expertise and a superior level of service, enables us to be extremely competitive and maintain quick delivery times. We supply manufacturers all over the world which include spinners of weaving, knitting, upholstery and carpet yarns, as well as felt-makers, technical non-woven and home-ware manufacturers. We collaborate with industry partners, brands, and farmers to develop cutting-edge products that meet the evolving demands of the market. From research and development to creating eco-friendly and traceable solutions, our projects are focused on driving progress in the wool industry. Explore how we’re working to improve product quality, sustainability, and transparency throughout the supply chain. Product Development. Farm Traceability. Regional Logos. Product Development. Driving demand for British wool through new products is a crucial part of our activity. This helps increase demand for our product and in turn helps increase the price of the wool. During the past 12 months we have been working with our supply chain partners and have consolidated and developed an industry sourcing guide of British wool yarns targeting the fashion sector. These are available to view within our Trade section. Trade. Traceable Wool. Greater Value for Your Wool. Since 2021, all wool handled and sold by British Wool is fully traceable back to our members’ farms. This means we can connect wool from the finished product right back to the farmers who produced it. As more brands and consumers want to know where their products come from, demand for traceable British wool is growing. This creates an opportunity to add value to the wool our members produce. What Does Traceability Mean for You? When a brand is looking for specific traceable wool, we identify suitable wool lots that meet their requirements. This means traceable wool is driven by market demand, so it isn’t something members can choose to opt into every year. Not every part of your clip will necessarily qualify. Brands may request particular wool grades, qualities or specifications, so only wool that meets these requirements can be included in a traceable lot. If your wool is selected for a traceable lot, it can achieve a premium above the standard auction price. This additional value is passed directly back to you as a member and will be shown on your wool payment receipt. Growing Demand for Traceable British Wool. Demand for traceable wool is continuing to grow, particularly from the sleep industry. Last season, we sold 770,000kg of traceable wool to customers including Woolroom, Harrison Spinks and Dreams. Since the scheme launched, we have sold more than 2.5 million kilos of traceable wool. Today, 15 brands purchase traceable British wool, with demand continuing to increase. Grown Here. Graded Here. Traceable Back to You. Our regional wool labels help showcase the journey of your wool. From the farm where it was grown, through grading, and into the products it becomes. Each regional label identifies wool that has been grown and graded within the same UK home nation, giving greater visibility of where the fibre comes from and strengthening the connection between the finished product and the farmers who produced it. For our members, this means your wool can be recognised not only as British wool, but for its regional origin and provenance. What does this mean for our members? Regional certification helps: Showcase where your wool comes from – connecting finished products back to the farms and regions where the wool was produced. Strengthen the value of regional wool – highlighting the distinct provenance and characteristics of wool from different parts of the UK. Keep more of the wool journey within the region – with wool grown and professionally graded within the same home nation. Give customers greater confidence in its provenance – providing clear, independently certified traceability from farm through to finished product. Support the wider farming community – by celebrating the contribution of sheep farmers and the landscapes they manage. Secret Link.

We’ve dedicated ourselves to crafting. beautiful and durable wool carpets. for a broad range of commercial environments,. without compromise. About us. Part of the fabric and heritage of the country. While we continue to invest in state of the art, high-speed looms and technology to improve business efficiency, there are some parts of the Wilton story we cling on to: we still weave all of our carpet on the same site we started on, 300 years ago; we continue to use British wool, renowned for it’s hardy durability; and we maintain a relentless attention to the quality of what we produce so we continue to live up to our enduring reputation. About Us. British wool. Sheep have evolved to produce one of the most effective natural forms of all-weather protection. And because of our famously intemperate weather, British sheep produce one of the hardiest of wools. It’s renewable, biodegradable, and a natural insulator; wool absorbs and releases humidity, and can reduce floating dust particles, trapping them in the fibres until they can be safely vacuumed and disposed of, meaning wool carpets help enhance the internal environment. Using homegrown wool reduces our product miles, lessens our environmental impact, supports British growers and improves certainty of supply. About Us. Outstanding service and support – we’re here for every step. Carpet is a technical part of an interior scheme, and from our project consultants to designers; weavers to the quality inspection team, the whole process is looked after by dedicated specialists who bring their experience and professionalism to each job. We love what we do, from meeting people equally passionate about their work, getting to know beautiful buildings, the creative process and the hum of our busy factory in the heart of Wiltshire. We’d be happy to hear from you and develop an understanding of your project. Get in touch! About Us. Ethos, accreditations and affiliations. We’re dependent on British sheep and the grass they graze on across this country. We’re also based within a rural conservation area straddling three shallow, chalk-bedded rivers that are home to a great variety of wildlife. This area has been designated a site of Special Scientific Interest (SSI) so represents our ethos to be safe, clean and protective of our environment. We’re proud to be ISO 14001 certified. Our other partnerships reflect our commitment to quality, International standards, as well as cooperation with respected industry bodies and the sharing of expertise and best practice. Your Basket.

Top 9 Carpet Manufacturers in the UK: Leading British Carpet Brands for 2026. The UK has a long-established carpet manufacturing industry, combining traditional weaving skills with modern production technology, innovative materials and contemporary design. From luxurious wool carpets for elegant homes to hard-wearing flooring for hotels, offices and public buildings, British carpet manufacturers offer a wide variety of products for different interiors and budgets. Choosing the right carpet manufacturer involves more than comparing colours and prices. Buyers should consider material quality, manufacturing expertise, durability, available designs, warranties and the suitability of each product for its intended environment. In this guide, we explore nine established carpet manufacturers serving the UK market, covering woven carpets, British wool, synthetic flooring and commercial carpet solutions. 1. Brintons Carpets. Location: Kidderminster, Worcestershire, England. Primary Products: Axminster woven carpets, Wilton woven carpets, wool-rich carpets and bespoke carpet designs. Customer Ratings & Reputation: Brintons has a long-established reputation for woven carpet craftsmanship, traditional design expertise and premium flooring. The company traces its history back to 1783 and serves both residential and commercial markets. Why They Rank #1: Brintons stands out for its specialisation in woven carpets, particularly Axminster and Wilton constructions. Its combination of heritage, design development and manufacturing expertise makes it a strong choice for buyers seeking premium woven carpets. Its wool-rich collections are suitable for homeowners who value traditional craftsmanship, as well as designers working on hotels and other prestigious projects. Website: https://www.brintons.co.uk/. 2. Axminster Carpets. Location: Axminster, Devon, England. Primary Products: Axminster woven carpets, bespoke carpets, patterned carpets and premium residential and commercial flooring. Customer Ratings & Reputation: Axminster Carpets is associated with a long history of British carpet weaving. The company traces its origins to 1755 and is known for traditional craftsmanship and specialist carpet production. Why They Rank #2: Axminster Carpets is notable for its traditional woven manufacturing expertise and bespoke design capabilities. Axminster-style carpets are valued for their ability to reproduce detailed patterns and create distinctive interior schemes. The company is worth considering for luxury homes, hospitality projects, heritage properties and buyers looking for customised carpet designs rather than standard mass-market styles. Website: https://www.axminster-carpets.co.uk/. 3. Cormar Carpets. Location: Lancashire, England. Primary Products: Wool twist carpets, wool loop carpets, synthetic carpets, deep-pile carpets and easy-clean carpet collections. Customer Ratings & Reputation: Cormar has been designing and manufacturing carpets since 1956. The company supplies carpet retailers across the UK and Ireland and offers collections covering different styles, materials and household requirements. Why They Rank #3: Cormar earns its place through its long manufacturing history, broad residential product range and UK production capabilities. Its collections include traditional wool-based options alongside practical synthetic carpets for everyday living. For homeowners, the range makes it easier to compare texture, comfort, appearance and maintenance requirements within one manufacturer's portfolio. Cormar is a strong option for living rooms, bedrooms, stairs and other domestic spaces where appearance and practicality both matter. Website: https://www.cormarcarpets.co.uk/. 4. Ulster Carpets. Location: Portadown, County Armagh, Northern Ireland. Primary Products: Luxury woven carpets, Axminster carpets, bespoke carpet designs and residential and hospitality flooring. Customer Ratings & Reputation: Established in 1938, Ulster Carpets is a family-owned business with a longstanding reputation for carpet manufacturing. The company emphasises design quality, specialist weaving and its heritage in carpet production. Why They Rank #4: Ulster Carpets is an important name for buyers seeking premium woven flooring and carefully developed designs. Its products serve homes and hospitality environments, where appearance, consistency and long-term performance can be particularly important. Its manufacturing expertise makes it relevant to architects, interior designers, hotel operators and homeowners who want a more distinctive carpet than a basic plain or textured floor covering. Website: https://ulstercarpets.com/. 5. Brockway Carpets. Location: Kidderminster, Worcestershire, England. Primary Products: Wool carpets, wool-rich carpets, loop-pile carpets, textured carpets and traditional and contemporary carpet designs. Customer Ratings & Reputation: Brockway is a family-run carpet manufacturer known for its emphasis on wool and British craftsmanship. The company highlights its use of British wool and its longstanding carpet-making expertise. Why They Rank #5: Brockway is a strong choice for customers who prioritise natural materials, traditional manufacturing skills and the distinctive feel of wool carpet. Wool can offer warmth, comfort and a naturally textured finish, making it popular in bedrooms, living rooms and other residential spaces. The company is also worth exploring for buyers who prefer British-made products and want a selection of classic and modern designs rather than a purely synthetic carpet range. Website: https://www.brockway.co.uk/. 6. Abingdon Flooring. Location: United Kingdom. Primary Products: Synthetic carpets, polypropylene carpets, polyester carpets, twist carpets, stain-resistant carpets and residential flooring collections. Customer Ratings & Reputation: Abingdon Flooring is a British carpet manufacturer offering a wide range of residential carpet products. Its portfolio includes practical carpet collections and products marketed with stain-related guarantees and wear warranties, subject to individual product terms. Why They Rank #6: Abingdon Flooring is a notable option for households looking for practical carpets in a wide choice of colours, styles and price points. Its ranges include carpets designed for busy homes, with product features intended to simplify cleaning and everyday maintenance. The company is particularly relevant to families, landlords and homeowners comparing synthetic carpet options for bedrooms, living rooms, stairs and other frequently used spaces. Buyers should check the specifications and warranty conditions of each individual range before purchasing. Website: https://www.abingdonflooring.co.uk/. 7. Cavalier Carpets. Location: Lancashire, England. Primary Products: Wool carpets, synthetic carpets, twist carpets, loop carpets, commercial carpets and bespoke carpet solutions. Customer Ratings & Reputation: Cavalier is a British carpet manufacturer with a longstanding presence in the industry. The company serves residential and commercial markets and offers a range of carpet styles through its retail network. Why They Rank #7: Cavalier Carpets offers a combination of British manufacturing, established industry experience and a varied product portfolio. Its residential collections cater to different interior styles, while its commercial products provide options for projects requiring tailored designs and specific performance characteristics. This makes Cavalier worth considering for homeowners, interior designers and commercial buyers looking for a manufacturer with both standard collections and more specialised carpet solutions. Website: https://www.cavaliercarpets.co.uk/. 8. Victoria Carpets. Location: United Kingdom. Primary Products: Wool carpets, synthetic carpets, traditional woven styles and contemporary residential carpet collections. Customer Ratings & Reputation: Victoria Carpets traces its history to 1895 and has a longstanding connection with the British carpet industry. The brand is associated with a variety of carpet styles, including wool and synthetic options. Why They Rank #8: Victoria Carpets deserves consideration for its heritage, established manufacturing identity and variety of carpet styles. Its collections include options for customers seeking traditional wool flooring as well as easier-care products for modern homes. The brand is useful for buyers comparing different carpet constructions and finishes through a company with a long presence in the UK market. Website: https://www.victoriacarpets.com/. 9. Penthouse Carpets. Location: Kidderminster, Worcestershire, England. Primary Products: British-made wool carpets, wool-rich carpets and residential carpet collections. Customer Ratings & Reputation: Penthouse Carpets promotes its British-made wool carpet collections and employee-owned business model. The company highlights the quality of its wool products and its focus on comfort and durability. Why They Rank #9: Penthouse Carpets is a worthwhile choice for homeowners who prefer wool flooring and want to explore carpet styles produced by an established British manufacturer. Its focus on wool gives buyers an alternative to synthetic carpet collections, particularly for rooms where a natural appearance and comfortable underfoot feel are priorities. Customers should compare individual product specifications, pile construction, suitability and care instructions before selecting a particular range. Website: https://penthousecarpets.co.uk/. How to Choose the Right UK Carpet Manufacturer. The best manufacturer for your project depends on the type of room, your budget, the carpet material and how much wear the flooring will need to withstand. 1. Choose the Right Material. Wool carpets are popular for their natural feel, warmth and appearance. Synthetic options, including polypropylene and polyester, can offer practical choices for households that prioritise easy maintenance or particular stain-resistance features. Compare the specifications of the actual product rather than relying on the material name alone. 2. Consider the Room and Its Traffic. Bedrooms may suit soft, comfortable carpet styles, while stairs, hallways and busy family rooms generally require careful attention to durability and suitability. Commercial projects may need products designed for the demands of hotels, offices or public buildings. 3. Compare Warranties and Care Requirements. Check the warranty period, exclusions, cleaning instructions and installation requirements. A stain guarantee is not necessarily the same as a general wear warranty, so read the terms for the specific carpet range. 4. Look at Design and Construction. Woven carpets, twist carpets and loop-pile carpets have different appearances and performance characteristics. Request samples where possible so you can assess the colour, texture and finish in your own lighting. 5. Check Availability Through Authorised Retailers. Many manufacturers sell through flooring retailers rather than directly to consumers. Use the company's official website to find a local stockist, request samples and obtain product information before making a purchase. Final Thoughts. The UK carpet industry offers a wide range of choices, from luxury woven carpets by Brintons and Axminster Carpets to practical residential collections from Cormar, Abingdon Flooring and other established manufacturers. For buyers seeking premium woven designs, Brintons, Axminster Carpets and Ulster Carpets are strong starting points. Those comparing wool-focused collections may also want to explore Brockway and Penthouse, while Cormar, Abingdon Flooring, Cavalier Carpets and Victoria Carpets offer further options across different styles and materials. Before deciding, compare samples, specifications, warranties, maintenance requirements and retailer availability. The right carpet is the one that suits your space, expected use and budget—not simply the one attached to the most familiar brand name. Its LVT collections provide decorative options for a range of interiors, while its commercial vinyl products address the needs of workplaces, healthcare facilities, education buildings and other high-use environments. The company also manufactures linoleum, which is a different material from vinyl despite sometimes being grouped with resilient flooring. This broader portfolio allows specifiers to compare products according to appearance, maintenance, performance and project requirements. Forbo provides technical resources and product documentation that can support architects, contractors and facilities managers during the specification process. Website: https://www.forbo.com/flooring/en-uk/. 6. Tarkett. Location: International manufacturer with dedicated UK residential and commercial flooring operations. Primary Products: Luxury Vinyl Tiles, click and glue-down LVT, sheet vinyl, homogeneous vinyl, heterogeneous vinyl, safety flooring and acoustic flooring. Customer Ratings & Reputation: Tarkett is an established international flooring manufacturer offering products across several flooring categories. Its UK operations provide residential and commercial collections for customers with different design and performance requirements. Why They Rank #6: Tarkett's broad portfolio makes it particularly relevant to projects that require more than one type of flooring. Its LVT collections include different formats and installation options, while its commercial vinyl products are designed for applications such as healthcare, education, offices, hospitality and retail. Some product ranges focus on decorative finishes, while others are developed for demanding environments where durability, cleaning and acoustic performance are important. Buyers can use Tarkett's technical documentation to compare the characteristics of individual collections. The company also publishes information about sustainability and material-related initiatives, which may be useful to customers evaluating flooring specifications for larger projects. Website: https://www.tarkett.co.uk/. 7. Gerflor. Location: International manufacturer with a dedicated UK market presence. Primary Products: Luxury Vinyl Tiles, vinyl sheet flooring, homogeneous vinyl, heterogeneous vinyl, safety flooring, sports flooring and specialist commercial floor coverings. Customer Ratings & Reputation: Gerflor is an international manufacturer specialising in resilient flooring and related surface solutions. Its UK portfolio serves both residential and commercial markets, with products for a variety of interior applications. Why They Rank #7: Gerflor offers a wide range of vinyl flooring products, making it relevant to customers comparing decorative residential flooring with specialist commercial solutions. Its residential collections include vinyl planks, tiles and sheet flooring designed to provide different appearances and practical features. For commercial projects, the company offers specialist products for environments such as healthcare facilities, offices, hospitality venues and sports spaces. Gerflor is worth considering when the flooring specification needs to account for more than appearance alone. Depending on the selected product, important factors may include slip resistance, acoustic performance, cleaning requirements and suitability for the intended traffic levels. Website: https://www.gerflor.co.uk/. 8. IVC Commercial. Location: International manufacturing and supply operations serving the UK commercial flooring market. Primary Products: Heterogeneous sheet vinyl, compact vinyl flooring, acoustic vinyl flooring, safety flooring, commercial LVT and carpet tiles. Customer Ratings & Reputation: IVC Commercial is part of the wider Unilin flooring group and specialises in flooring for commercial and public environments. Its portfolio includes products developed for sectors such as housing, healthcare, education, offices, hospitality and retail. Why They Rank #8: IVC Commercial is a relevant option for customers seeking practical flooring solutions for larger commercial projects. Its sheet vinyl collections include options designed to balance appearance, durability, installation requirements and maintenance. Depending on the product, acoustic, safety and other performance characteristics may also be important considerations. The company's range extends beyond vinyl sheet flooring into other commercial flooring categories, making it useful for contractors, architects and specifiers comparing products for different areas of the same building. IVC Commercial provides product information and technical documentation to support selection and specification. Website: https://www.ivc-commercial.com/en-gb/. How to Choose the Right Vinyl or LVT Flooring Manufacturer. Selecting the right flooring manufacturer starts with understanding where the flooring will be installed and what the space requires. 1. Decide Between LVT and Sheet Vinyl. LVT is supplied in individual tiles or planks and is often selected for its realistic wood, stone and decorative designs. Sheet vinyl is supplied in rolls and can be suitable for areas where a continuous floor covering is preferred. Neither format is automatically better for every project. The right choice depends on the room, installation method, appearance and performance requirements. 2. Consider Residential or Commercial Use. Residential flooring priorities may include appearance, comfort, cleaning and suitability for everyday household use. Commercial installations may require additional consideration of traffic levels, slip resistance, hygiene, acoustic performance, fire classification and other technical requirements. Always check the specifications for the exact product being considered. 3. Compare Installation Methods. Some LVT products use adhesive, while others use click-lock or alternative installation systems. Sheet vinyl also has specific subfloor preparation and installation requirements. Installation method can influence preparation costs, fitting time and the suitability of a product for a particular room. 4. Review Durability and Maintenance. Look at the product's wear layer, overall construction, recommended cleaning methods and warranty terms. For commercial projects, review the relevant technical data and suitability for the expected traffic. Do not assume that all products within a manufacturer's range offer the same level of performance. 5. Check Certifications and Technical Documentation. For projects with specific requirements, review the manufacturer's technical documents, applicable product standards, test information and declarations. Healthcare, education, hospitality and other commercial projects may require particular performance characteristics that ordinary residential flooring does not provide. 6. Request Samples and Compare Designs. Colour and texture can look different under showroom lighting compared with natural light at home or in a commercial building. Request samples where available and compare them with the room's lighting, furniture, wall colours and overall design. 7. Confirm Warranty and Local Availability. Check whether the product is available through an authorised retailer or distributor in your area. Review warranty conditions, installation requirements and any exclusions before making a purchase. For international manufacturers, local distribution and technical support can also influence the overall buying experience. Final Thoughts. The UK vinyl and LVT flooring market offers options for a wide range of residential and commercial requirements. Amtico and Karndean are particularly relevant to buyers exploring design-led luxury vinyl flooring. Polyflor and Altro offer strong options for commercial projects where technical performance and specialist requirements are important. Forbo, Tarkett, Gerflor and IVC Commercial provide broader portfolios covering different resilient flooring categories and applications. The best choice depends on the intended use, budget, appearance, installation method and performance requirements of the project. Comparing technical specifications and product samples is an important step before choosing a particular collection. Whether you are renovating a home, specifying flooring for an office or planning a larger commercial installation, researching the manufacturer and the individual product can help you make a more informed decision.
